title: HTML & CSS
desc: Build your first responsive website, one element at a time.
body:
A website is a collection of pages. Your browser requests those pages from a server and displays them. HTML gives a page structure, CSS controls its appearance, and JavaScript adds interaction.
Practice: open a website and identify a heading, a paragraph, and a link.

Create a folder called my-first-site. Open it in VS Code and create index.html. Add the code below, then open the file in your browser. CODE:

Hello, world!

I am learning with Bright Tech Solutions.

Visit Bright Tech Practice: change the heading to your name.

title: JavaScript
desc: Bring your websites to life with practical interactions.

title: Python Programming
desc: Start solving problems with readable, practical code.
body:
Python is a programming language used for automation, applications and data work. A print statement displays output.
CODE:print('Hello, Bright Tech!')
Practice: save this as hello.py and run it in a Python environment.

Conditional statements choose which instructions to run. Indentation is part of Python syntax.
CODE:score = 75
if score >= 50:
    print('Passed')
else:
    print('Try again')
Practice: change score to 40 and run the code again.

A for loop repeats instructions for each item in a sequence.
CODE:for topic in ['HTML', 'CSS', 'Python']:
    print(topic)
Practice: replace the list with three things you want to learn.

title: UI/UX Design
desc: Create clear, useful digital experiences for real people.
body:
Start with a user and a task. Ask what they want to achieve, what stops them, and what a successful outcome looks like.
Practice: interview a learner about finding the next lesson in a course.

A user flow lists the steps needed to complete a task. For course learning: open My Learning, choose a course, choose a lesson, study, mark complete.
Practice: sketch these steps and note where a learner might get stuck.

A wireframe is a simple layout without decorative details. Put the most useful information and main action where people can find them.
Practice: sketch a mobile lesson page with a title, lesson content, and a completion button.

title: Graphic Design
desc: Communicate ideas through thoughtful visual design.
body:
Visual hierarchy helps viewers see the most important information first. Use size, spacing and weight to separate a headline, supporting details and a call to action.
Practice: sketch a poster for an HTML lesson.

Colour supports recognition and readability. Check that text remains readable against its background and avoid relying on colour alone to communicate meaning.
Practice: compare white and grey text on a purple background.

Start with a purpose, an audience, and one main message. Add a clear title, the essential details and a next step.
Practice: design a poster inviting learners to watch a tutorial on the Bright Tech YouTube channel.

title: Web Development
desc: Connect structure, styling and interaction in one project.
body:
Define the site's audience and main action before writing code. Sketch the content sections and navigation.
Practice: plan a personal portfolio with an introduction, projects and contact information.

Build the structure with semantic HTML, add layout and styling with CSS, and use JavaScript where interaction is useful.
Practice: create a portfolio page with a heading, project cards and working contact links.

Test your site at several widths. Check for horizontal overflow, readable text, useful spacing and controls you can operate with a keyboard.
Practice: resize your browser to a phone-sized width and fix one layout problem.

title: Programming Fundamentals
desc: Learn the thinking behind every programming language.
body:
Break a large task into small steps. An algorithm is a sequence of instructions to solve a problem.
Practice: write the steps for calculating the average of three numbers.

A program accepts inputs, processes them and produces outputs. Identify each part before choosing a language.
Practice: for a grade calculator, list the inputs, calculation and expected output.

Debugging means finding and fixing mistakes. Reproduce the problem, compare the actual and expected results, and check one small part at a time.
Practice: test your average algorithm with 3, 6 and 9. The expected answer is 6.
